chunks: And it is narrated from Burayd al-‘Ijli, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I owe a debt to orphans, and I fear that if I sell my estate, I will be left with nothing.”
He عليه السلام said: “Do not sell your estate; rather, give some and keep some.”

key_terms.دَيْنًا: a financial debt or liability owed
key_terms.لِأَيْتَامٍ: to orphans, indicating vulnerable rightful claimants

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he owes money to orphans but fears losing everything by selling his property?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a financial dilemma involving a debt owed to orphans and the preservation of one’s livelihood. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام instructs that the debtor should not dispose of the entire estate, but should pay part and retain part, indicating a balanced approach to fulfilling obligations without self-destruction.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3693 - It is narrated from Burayd Al-Ijli who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (as), "I owe a debt to orphans, and I fear that if I sell my estate, I will be left with nothing."
Imam (as) said: "Do not sell your estate; rather, give some and keep some."
